text: Stock futures rebounded after Friday's tech-led rout: Nasdaq-100 futures were up about 3–3.6% and S&P 500 futures about 2.2–2.9% before the open, led by chipmakers.
Gold bounced about 2.3% to near $3,618 by 8 AM ET after Friday's slide to a 14-month low, trading between $3,540 and $3,638 overnight.
Silver rose about 2.8% to near $42.28, nudging the gold/silver ratio down from 86 to about 85.6.
Treasury yields climbed as money left bonds: the 10-year rose about 4 bp to 4.96% and the 2-year about 7 bp to 4.69%, with traders pricing about a 96% chance of a December Fed hike.
The yen weakened about 0.3–0.4% to near 159.1 per dollar, giving back part of Friday's gain and staying close to the 160 level.
Brent slipped about 1.6% to near $91.11 as worries about global growth outweighed Middle East shipping risks.
Bitcoin recovered to about $61,100 after hitting about $55,130 on Saturday, its weakest level since September 2024.
